title: the detached-context rule reads the resolved member symbol, not the member's name: a `context` member on an ordinary value stays ordinary, and a type position naming the real one is not a detachment
notes: specification/requirements.mdx, 'Context Access': '`Capability.context()` MUST be an inherited, compiler-recognized call on subclasses of `Context`.' `SMITHERS2107` refuses a detached reference to THAT member; `context` is an ordinary identifier and nothing reserves it, so this is the other direction. It guards four distinct ways the refusal could over-fire, and each line is one of them. Line 2 detaches `context` from a plain object literal and calls it: a rule keyed on the member's NAME turns this red. Line 3 detaches a static named `context` from an ordinary class — the shape closest to a capability without being one, and the one a rule keyed on 'a static member named context of a class' would catch. Line 4 reaches the same plain object through `Reflect.get(holder, "context")`: the reflective spellings are refused BY NAME AND KEY on a Context subclass, which is exactly the kind of enumeration that over-fires, so the identical call on a non-capability has to stay ordinary. Line 5 is the type-position exemption: `type ContextReader = typeof Reader.context` names the real compiler-recognized member of the real capability, in a type annotation, where nothing is read and no callable value escapes — this is the one line of the case that touches the capability's own member, and it is the one an implementation is most likely to refuse, because the syntax is identical to the refused spelling and only the POSITION differs. Line 1 keeps the sound direct call alive in the same program so the case cannot pass by the rule being absent altogether. Running it matters rather than merely compiling: `detachedFromObject()` and `detachedFromClass()` are invoked with no receiver, so a lowering that rewrote a detached `context` reference into something receiver-dependent would produce a program that compiles and dies, which is a class this corpus has been bitten by before and which only an `output` case can see. WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES NOT PIN: `Reflect.get` on the CAPABILITY, which is refused and belongs to `a-detached-context-reference-is-rejected`'s family; and it makes no claim that the reflective enumeration is complete — a computed key is a recorded open residual on both backends. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the fifth declared stdout line from `type-only` to `value` turns the case red on BOTH backends with the stdout diff printed, and the expectation was restored byte-identically (sha256 f695393885e013d67142c48be1aaa1ad265fb213e1386827217fcae661f4a8ef before and after). That line is the type-position one, which is the guard this case exists for and the one an over-correction breaks first.
